name: Lifecycle and access stage
summary: What a project allows over time: the access stage derived from status and dates, automatic archiving and deletion, and the manual archive and delete actions.

roles.note: Manual deletion has its own authority check (canDeleteProject) rather than a permission string. Support users can bypass access-stage gating.

actions.note: Needs a reason and passes canDeleteProject

nfr.statement: Today approved projects are archived automatically at their planned end and marked deleted 365 days later. Whether data is physically removed is not shown.
nfr.open_question: What retention do customers expect after a project ends, and is it contractual (DEC-019)?

requirements.title: Access stage comes from status first, then dates
requirements.statement: Draft and Pending-approval projects are in Pre-Setup, and Archived or Deleted status wins as stored. For every other status, dates decide: - more than 30 days before the start date: Pre-Setup - within 30 days of the start: Setup - from the start until start plus duration (in months): In-construction - for 365 days after that: Archived - after that: Deleted Construction phase is a separate field and is not used.

sources.title: Direct code reads during USER migration (2026-10-29)

open_checks: Durations truncate to whole months; month addition uses runtime-local Date.setMonth, while the archive jobs use date-fns addMonths; there is no project-local midnight

requirements.title: Actions are gated by access stage as well as permission
requirements.statement: Each project action allows only certain access stages (setup actions need Setup or In-construction, for example), checked separately from the user's permission. A missing project ID is a bad request, an unknown project is not found, and a disallowed stage is forbidden. Support users can bypass the stage check on routes that allow it.

acceptance_criteria.given: A project admin on a project in Pre-Setup
acceptance_criteria.when: They try to change a user's role
acceptance_criteria.then: The request is forbidden because of the stage, even though they hold the permission

requirements.title: Projects archive and delete themselves automatically
requirements.statement: Once approved, a project is set to Archived on its planned end date (start plus duration). It is set to Deleted 365 days later, if it is still Approved or Archived. Project admins are emailed 30 and 7 days before each step, and each step is logged. The jobs are rescheduled when dates change.

acceptance_criteria.given: An approved 6-month project that started 1 March
acceptance_criteria.then: Admins are emailed on 2 August and 25 August, and the project becomes Archived on 1 September
Its status becomes Deleted, with reason "Deleted by System"

requirements.title: The archive endpoint replaces the project with a renamed copy
requirements.statement: The project-api archive action is not a reversible flag. It creates a copy with a suffixed ID and name and status Deleted, then deletes the original record. The automatic archive (PROJ-REQ-016) only changes the status.
open_checks: The business meaning of archive, delete and restore must be approved before this changes; moving child references and restoring are not shown

acceptance_criteria.then: (Current behaviour) P1 no longer exists, and a Deleted project with a suffixed ID and name takes its place

requirements.title: Deleting a project needs a reason
requirements.statement: Deleting a project needs a reason of 1 to 1000 characters and the caller must pass the delete-authority check. The project is replaced by a suffixed Deleted copy, roles and groups are cleaned up, support is assigned and people are notified.
open_checks: Failed assignment, status or deletion steps across embedded users, role assignments, groups, preferences, counts and child references are not traced

acceptance_criteria.given: A user allowed to delete project P
acceptance_criteria.when: They delete it with an empty reason
